assignments.name: brandFacts
assignments.value:
- ABC Company is a leading provider of innovative solutions in the technology industry.
- Our company has been at the forefront of technological advancement since its inception in 2005.
- Family story (tell it as a family story, not as documented history): when the company began, it was just a small startup with a vision to revolutionize the way people interact with technology. The founder was given the opportunity to turn this vision into reality.
- The company sits at the intersection of creativity and technology, fostering an environment where innovation thrives.
- Varieties: cutting-edge software solutions and hardware products. 100% customer-focused.
- The products are developed by a team of dedicated professionals.
- ABC Company LLC is based in San Francisco, California. We develop and ship our products globally.
- Three product lines of the same category: basic, standard and premium. Each line offers unique features and benefits. 12 oz packages, also sold as 2-packs and 3-packs.
- Standard and premium lines also come as compatible accessories.
- Basic line tastes of simplicity and reliability, with a user-friendly interface and robust performance.
- Standard line tastes of enhanced functionality and improved aesthetics, with a smooth user experience and a modern design.
- Premium line tastes of luxury and exclusivity, with a high-end build quality and advanced features.
- Shipping: free on every subscription order and on one-time orders over $55. We sell to customers in the United States.
- Subscriptions: delivery weekly, every two weeks or monthly. Subscribers get free shipping (there is no percentage discount). Pause, skip or cancel anytime.
- Caffeine: our products have not been lab-tested. It is in the normal range for 100% customer-focused products.
- Never say about ABC Company: prices, review scores, "organic" or any certification, awards, "lab-tested", "roasted to order", "AA", cooperatives or partner companies.

assignments.name: imageStyle
assignments.value:
Photorealistic editorial food photograph for a specialty coffee brand's blog. It must look like a real photograph taken by a professional, not an illustration or a 3D render.

Camera: full-frame camera, 50mm lens (85mm for close-ups), aperture around f/2.8 to f/4, the main subject in sharp focus with a soft, natural background blur.
Light: soft natural daylight from a window at one side, gentle shadows, no flash, no studio glare.
Color: deep coffee browns, warm cream and beige (#EDE4D3), matte black, with small accents of brass or gold and ripe-cherry red. Natural, slightly warm white balance. Not oversaturated.
Surfaces and props: dark walnut or aged wood tabletop, natural linen, handmade ceramic cups in cream or matte black, clear glass servers, brushed steel or brass tools. Everything plain and unbranded.
Composition: one clear subject, uncluttered, generous empty space, rule of thirds.
Texture: true to life. Crema on espresso, fine steam, an oily sheen on dark-roast beans, a dry matte surface on light-roast beans, visible grain in the wood.
Mood: calm, warm, unhurried morning. Crafted and premium, but homely.

Strictly none of these: text, letters, numbers, logos, labels, watermarks, brand names, printed packaging, people's faces, extra or malformed fingers, cartoon or illustration style, 3D-render look, HDR, heavy vignette, lens flare, sparkles, clutter, words drawn in latte art.

parameters.content:
## Weekly blog post from the topic queue
Takes the next **Queued** row from the Google Sheet, researches it, writes the post, makes 3 images, saves everything in Shopify as a **hidden draft**, marks the row **Drafted** and emails you.

### Setup (once)
1. **Config**: set `shop` (the part before .myshopify.com) and `notifyEmail`. Check `blogHandle`.
2. **Google Sheets OAuth2** credential on the 2 Sheets nodes.
3. **SerpAPI** credential on "Google Search: What People Ask".
4. **Anthropic** credential on the 2 AI nodes.
5. **OpenAI** credential on "OpenAI: Generate Image".
6. **Shopify**: the app needs scopes `read_content`, `write_content`, `write_files`, `read_files`. If you add scopes to an existing app, release a new version and approve it on the store. Custom Auth credential on "Shopify: Get Access Token":
`{ "body": { "client_id": "...", "client_secret": "..." } }`
7. **Gmail** credential on the 2 Email nodes.
8. Click **Run manually (test)**, review the draft in Shopify, then Publish the workflow.

### 1. Queue and research
Picks the first row with status **Queued** (priority 1 first). Rows on **Hold** are skipped. Google shows what people ask; then the AI searches the web and reports facts with their sources. The writer may only use numbers found here.

### 2. Write the post, make the images
Voice, structure and accuracy rules are in **Build Writing Request**. Brand facts and the photo style are in **Config**. If image generation fails, the post is still saved without images.

### 3. Save as hidden draft, update the sheet, email
Images go to Shopify Files first. The post is saved with `isPublished: false`. The email lists every figure to check, automatic warnings, and the three images.

parameters.jsCode:
// Builds the research request from the picked sheet row. The AI searches the web itself
// and reports facts with their sources; the writer may only use numbers found there.
const cfg = $('Config').first().json;
const t = $('Pick Next Topic').first().json.topic;
const shopify = $input.first().json; // from Check Shopify Setup
const base = String(cfg.storeUrl).replace(/\/+$/, '');

// All AI calls go through OpenRouter, so the three model fields in Config must be OpenRouter model IDs.
const wrong = ['researchModel', 'writerModel', 'imageModel'].filter(k => !String(cfg[k] || '').includes('/'));
if (wrong.length) throw new Error('Config: ' + wrong.join(', ') + ' must be OpenRouter model IDs, which contain a slash. For example researchModel = anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5, writerModel = anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, imageModel = openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst.');

const today = $now.toFormat('d MMMM yyyy');

const system = [
  'You are the fact-checker and researcher for a coffee blog. A writer will use your notes to write the article described below, and may only state numbers that appear in your notes. Search the web and report what reliable sources say.',
  '',
  'SOURCES, in order of preference',
  '1. Official and scientific: FDA, USDA FoodData Central, NIH, EFSA, Health Canada, Mayo Clinic, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, peer-reviewed journals, university extension services.',
  '2. Coffee bodies: National Coffee Association (ncausa.org, aboutcoffee.org), Specialty Coffee Association, World Coffee Research, International Coffee Organization, Kenya\'s Agriculture and Food Authority (Coffee Directorate), Nairobi Coffee Exchange.',
  '3. Independent testing and edited publications with named authors: Consumer Reports, America\'s Test Kitchen, national newspapers, long-running food and coffee magazines.',
  '4. For a figure about one brand or chain, try in this order: (a) the company\'s own website, product page or nutrition page, searching for it by name; (b) a named independent lab test; (c) a caffeine database such as Caffeine Informer. Label every (c) figure "secondary database" and copy any caveat the page gives about how the figure was worked out.',
  'Do not use content farms, anonymous listicles, affiliate "best of" pages, forums, Pinterest, social posts, AI-generated summaries or ' + base.replace(/^https?:\/\//, '') + '.',
  '',
  'RULES',
  '- Report only what you read in the search results returned to you in this session. Never fill a gap from memory.',
  '- A long GAPS list is an acceptable result. A figure you are not sure of is not. If you cannot verify something the article needs, put it under GAPS and move on.',
  '- Every line under KEY FACTS, ANSWERS TO THE SEARCHES and BRAND FIGURES must contain the full URL (starting https://) of the page it came from, typed out in the line itself. A source name without its URL is useless to the writer. Do not use footnote numbers or link text in place of the URL, and do not rely on citations being attached automatically.',
  '- Give every figure with its unit and serving size. Give the date the page shows, or write "no date shown". Never guess a date.',
  '- You may add a simple conversion (per ounce, oz to ml) so servings can be compared. Mark it "calculated".',
  '- When sources disagree, give both figures and say so.',
  '- If any single serving you list is above the FDA\'s daily guidance for adults, include that guidance too.',
  '- For brands and chains, prefer ones sold in the United States.',
  '- Searches that mean the same thing get one answer. Group them.',
  '- Paraphrase. No quotation longer than 15 words.',
  '',
  'OUTPUT: plain text under these four headings, in this order. Keep each line short.',
  'KEY FACTS',
  '- <fact with unit and serving size> | <publisher> | <date shown, or "no date shown"> | <URL> | <note, if any: "calculated", "sources differ", "small study">',
  'ANSWERS TO THE SEARCHES',
  '- <search or group of searches>: <answer in one or two sentences> | <URL>',
  'BRAND FIGURES',
  '- <brand, product, serving size, figure> | <who published the figure> | <date shown> | <URL> | <"brand\'s own figure", "brand\'s figure as reported by <outlet>", "independent test" or "secondary database", plus any caveat in a few words>',
  '(write "not needed" under BRAND FIGURES when the article does not need other brands)',
  'GAPS',
  '- <what the writer must not state because it could not be verified>',
].join('\n');

const user = [
  'Today is ' + today + '. Readers are in the United States.',
  '',
  'ARTICLE TO RESEARCH',
  'Working title: ' + t.working_title,
  'Primary search phrase: ' + t.primary_keyword,
  'Brief: ' + t.brief,
  'Searches the article must answer: ' + (t.supporting_searches.join(' | ') || '(none listed)'),
  'Needs figures for other brands: ' + (t.names_other_brands ? 'YES. Find a sourced figure for each brand the brief or the searches call for. Five to ten well-sourced brands are enough.' : 'no'),
  'Health-sensitive: ' + (t.health_sensitive ? 'YES. For every health statement use only health authorities and published studies, and note the limits of each study (size, length, who was studied).' : 'no (ordinary care is enough)'),
].join('\n');


const request = {
  model: cfg.researchModel,
  max_tokens: 6000,
  reasoning: { effort: 'low', exclude: true }, // less thinking, and keep the thinking text and its signature out of the response
  messages: [{ role: 'system', content: system }, { role: 'user', content: user }],
  tools: [{ type: 'openrouter:web_search', parameters: { max_uses: Number(cfg.maxSearches) || 10, max_results: 5 } }],
};

// blogId and existingArticles are passed along unchanged because Parse Article and Assemble Draft read them from this node.
return [{ json: { request, today, blogId: shopify.blogId, blogHandle: shopify.blogHandle, existingArticles: shopify.existingArticles } }];
